title: Further Education During Unemployment
abstract: arXiv:2312.17123v5 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Evidence on the effectiveness of retraining unemployed U.S. workers primarily comes from evaluations of training programs, a narrow avenue for skill acquisition. We use administrative records from Ohio to estimate the effects of retraining, broadly defined as postsecondary enrollment, via matching. Our simple method bridges two strands of the dynamic treatment effect literature that differ in whether the counterfactual allows later treatment or rules it out throughout the treatment window. Enrollees experience earnings gains of six percent three to four years after enrolling, following depressed earnings during the first two years. The gains are driven by industry-switchers, particularly to healthcare.

translated_abstract: 关于美国失业工人再培训有效性的证据主要来自对培训项目的评估，而这只是技能获取的一条狭窄途径。我们利用俄亥俄州的行政记录，通过匹配方法来估计再培训的效果，这里的再培训被广义地定义为接受高等教育的入学。我们的简单方法连接了动态处理效应文献中的两个流派，这两个流派的区别在于反事实情形是否允许后续处理，还是在整个处理窗口期内排除后续处理。研究结果显示，入学者在入学后的头两年收入处于较低水平，但在入学三到四年后收入增长了6%。这些收益主要由转换行业的人群驱动，尤其是转向医疗保健行业的人。
tldr: 该研究利用俄亥俄州行政数据并通过匹配方法，将再培训广义化为接受高等教育入学，发现失业者入学者在经历前两年收入低迷后于三到四年后实现6%的收入增长，且收益主要来自转换行业者尤其是转向医疗行业的人。
en_tdlr: Using Ohio administrative records and a matching method that broadly defines retraining as postsecondary enrollment, this study finds that unemployed enrollees experience a six percent earnings gain three to four years after enrollment—following initially depressed earnings—with the gains driven mainly by industry-switchers, particularly those moving into healthcare.
